description:
The City of Parkland (City) offers a wide variety of events and activities throughout the year that serve residents of all ages and abilities. These events — ranging from seasonal festivals and cultural celebrations to inclusive awareness campaigns — often require high-quality amusement rides, bounce houses, and related services to ensure a safe, engaging, and memorable experience for the community. As such, selecting the right vendor is critical to the success and safety of these public gatherings.
Staff is requesting approval to issue a purchase order to Premier Bounce N Slide Party Rentals, LLC (Premier Bounce) for amusement rides, bounce houses, and related services for Fiscal Year 2027 for various events such as Light Up the Park, Snowfest, Parkland Day, Autism Awareness, and Splash Bash. Additionally, these services are utilized for summer camps and various youth activities throughout the year.
Premier Bounce has a proven history of successful collaboration with the City, consistently meeting expectations for safety, quality, and professionalism. Premier Bounce utilizes a centralized diesel power plant instead of multiple generators, which reduces noise levels and fire hazards, enhancing safety and operational efficiency. They also consistently deliver seasonal specialty inflatables, state-of-the-art carnival rides, and game trailers. Premier Bounce has the ability to provide a complete water supply system when needed, eliminating the need for coordination or third-party subcontracting. Their offerings, especially the autism-friendly inflatable, demonstrate a commitment to inclusivity which supports the City’s goals and initiatives for equitable community engagement.
In accordance with Procurement Code Sec. 2-142.14 Exempt Purchases, category (14) Arts and entertainment (artistic services, performing artists, entertainment and amusements at festivals or special events) are permitted. description:
The City of Parkland (City) Public Works Department has determined that the existing splash pad at Liberty Park has reached the end of its serviceable life. The City seeks a qualified design‑build firm of licensed, experienced professionals to provide all demolition, administration, design, permitting, equipment, materials, and construction services necessary to replace the splash pad located at Liberty Park, 9200 Ranch Road, Parkland.
The project includes demolition and removal of the existing splash pad and construction of a new approximately 2,000 square foot splash pad facility, including associated site improvements, utilities, fencing, drainage, and surfacing. The new splash pad will feature a “Liberty” themed design. The selected design-build firm shall be responsible for providing a complete turnkey project including conceptual design, final design, permitting, demolition, construction, inspections, testing, startup, and staff training necessary for a fully operational splash pad facility.
On July 6, 2026, in accordance with the City's Procurement Code, Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 2026-14, Liberty Park Splash Pad Design-Build Services, was advertised via the City's e-procurement platform, Planet Bids. On August 6, 2026, two (2) proposals were received: L Squared Enterprises, LLC, d/b/a L2 Aquatics, LLC, and Porter Contracting Services, LLC. L2 Aquatics, LLC, was rejected as they failed to attend the mandatory pre-bid meeting and failed to submit the required bid bond with their proposal.
On August 13, 2026, the Evaluation Committee reviewed the remaining proposal according to the published criteria. The Evaluation Committee was led by Felicia Trainer, Assistant Parks and Recreation Director, and included Jamorie Depusoir, Assistant Public Works Director for Projects, and Richard Spallino, Public Works Superintendent for Parks. The proposal was evaluated based on firm qualification, management and staff experience, technical approach and methodology, and proposed fees. After thorough review and discussion, the Evaluation Committee unanimously recommended the top ranked firm, Porter Contracting Services, LLC.
The City's Procurement Code, Section 2-141.4 for Approval Authorities and Methods, requires City Commission approval for purchases in excess of $50,000. If approved, the Purchasing Director will negotiate terms and conditions with Porter Contracting Services, LLC. The resulting agreement will be reviewed and approved by the City Attorney before execution.

City Commission (September 14, 2026) - A motion was made by Commissioner Isrow and seconded by Vice Mayor Brier to defer this item to the November 4, 2026, City Commission meeting. The motion passed 4-1, with Commissioner Kanterman dissenting.

description:
The City of Parkland (City) is seeking to develop the Village in the Park (VIP) commercial project. As such, Jones Lang LaSalle Americas, Inc. (JLL) was selected by the City Commission on August 13, 2025, via Resolution 2025-042, as the real estate agent to guide the City and to provide brokerage, marketing, advisory, and other associated services for the sale and development of approximately 34 acres of land owned by the City.
The process to secure a suitable developer comprises a two-step Request for Qualification (RFQ) and Request for Proposal (RFP). JLL initiated the RFQ solicitation request in December 2025 and closed that portion on January 19, 2026 with a total of ten (10) packages received. As part of the process of selecting a suitable partner for the commercial development project, the Commission selected five (5) qualified developers to then move to the RFP phase during the March 18, 2026 City Commission Workshop. The five (5) developers selected were Lincoln Property Company Commercial, The Georgetown Company, Turnberry Parkland Developer LLC, Edens, and Fuqua Development. Prior to the RFP submission deadline, Fuqua Development elected to withdraw from the RFP process with project site development costs as the cited reason.
JLL guided Commission through the procedural process with the remaining four (4) development firms prior to the interviews that took place with the developers on September 22, 2026 and September 23, 2026 at City Hall. Following the interviews and discussion with Commission, JLL provided a series of follow-up questions (Attachment A) to the developers and has compiled the developers' responses for consideration and discussion. This stage of the process is to focus on comparing each firm's overall alignment with the City's long-term vision for the VIP project and determining the preferred development firms to be identified as the finalists in the evaluation process. The outcome of this forthcoming phase will guide the Commission toward selecting the development team best positioned to deliver a successful and community-focused project.

description:
The City of Parkland (City) is requesting approval to award a purchase to The Sherwin‑Williams Company for three (3) Graco Line Lazer field paint stripers equipped with ride‑on attachments. These units will enhance the City’s ability to maintain high‑quality athletic field markings efficiently and safely.
Two of the stripers are included in the City’s established equipment replacement plan and will replace aging units currently deployed at Pine Trails Park and Terramar Park. Both existing units have reached the end of their useful lifecycle, demonstrating declining reliability and increased maintenance demands.
The third striper is a new purchase designated for Wedge Preserve Park. With athletic fields coming online at this location, the addition of a dedicated striping machine is essential to support regular field layout, maintenance, and event preparation without impacting service levels at other parks.
The Graco Line Lazer series with ride‑on attachments offers improved operator safety, enhanced efficiency, and more precise field striping. These units will reduce staff labor time, improve line accuracy, and support consistent field quality throughout the City’s park system.
Approval of this award will allow the City to move forward with ordering the equipment through The Sherwin‑Williams Company and ensure all three parks have reliable, high‑performance striping capabilities to meet daily operational and seasonal athletic needs.
On August 4, 2026, in accordance with the City's Procurement Code, Quote Request (QR) 2026-17, Field Striper with Ride-On Attachment, was advertised on PlanetBids, the Broward County Public Portal, and on the City's website. The QR was opened on August 12, 2026, and five (5) quotes were received: The Sherwin Williams Company, Pro-Grounds Products, Inc., Star-Seal of Florida, BSN Sports, LLC, and Mario Raymond and Company LLC d/b/a Pro Sports Equipment.
After careful review and evaluating the quotes in accordance with the requirements of the QR, staff recommends awarding the contract to the lowest responsive and responsible bid, The Sherwin Williams Company, in the amount of $61,380.
The City's Procurement Code, Section 2.141.4 Approval Authorities and Methods states that purchases in excess of $50,000 shall require City Commission approval. Staff recommends approval to purchase this equipment.

attachments.name: Resolution 2026-056 Refresh of the Audio Visual Equipment in City Commission Chambers

description:
The City of Parkland, Florida (the City) requires the services of a highly qualified firm with the expertise and resources to refresh the current audio visual equipment used for streaming of video from the City Hall Commission Chamber. The current audio visual equipment was initially procured in 2019 and is nearing the end of its service life. Refreshing the audio visual equipment will include the upgrade of broadcast video cameras, captioning equipment and software supporting fully managed streaming broadcasts, including installation services and equipment warranties (the Project).
A procurement team comprised of staff from the Information Technology Department, the City Clerks Office, and the Purchasing Department conducted market research and did not find any providers other than the incumbent vendor, capable of performing the Project. To further test the marketplace, on May 14, 2026, in accordance with the City's Procurement Code, Request for Information (RFI) 2026-12 for Fully Managed Commission Chamber Audio/Visual Production System and Hardware Refresh was issued via the City's e-procurement platform, Planet Bids. The RFI informed the vendor community of the City's intention to award a contract with the Granicus as the only provider uniquely positioned to provide this integrated solution. A total of 81 potential vendors received the RFI and only (1) response was received from AVI Systems, Inc., d/b/a Forte. The Forte response was reviewed by the Information Technology Department staff and found to rely on a combination of multiple third-party products and services rather than the single turn-key operational model of the Incumbent and was therefore determined to be unacceptable. Based on market research and the results of RFI 2026-12, a Sole Source/Brand Purchase was approved for Granicus on July 8, 2026 for the Project.
A proposal for the Project was received from Granicus on August 31, 2026. The proposal also included recurring services required to produce fully managed audio and visual broadcasts of commission meetings which will be provided for separately from this equipment purchase.
The City's Procurement Code, Section 2-141.4 Approval Authorities and Methods states that purchases in excess of $50,000 shall require City Commission approval.

description:
The City of Parkland experiences multiple ZIP Code inconsistencies, in which the ZIP Codes 33067 and 33076 are assigned not only to Parkland but also to Pompano Beach and Coral Springs. These inconsistencies can confuse residents, businesses, visitors, emergency responders, and governmental agencies when purposes such as emergency response coordination, insurance rate determinations, demographic reporting, and the efficiency of mail delivery are impacted by such inconsistencies.
United States Senate Bill S.4505, 119th Congress, is federal legislation that would require the United States Postal Service to designate ZIP Codes for certain communities, including Parkland, and establish a federal process to address longstanding ZIP Code designation issues affecting municipalities across the United States.
Resolution 2026-059 represents support for, and a meaningful step toward, clarity for more accurately reflected municipal boundaries.

description:
The proposed amendments provide limited flexibility to the City of Parkland ("City’") parking and vehicular use area landscaping standards for Educational and Vocational Institutions as well as Places of Worship ("Eligible Uses"). Specifically, the amendments would allow parking spaces serving Educational and Vocational Institutions and Places of Worship to be reduced from the standard 10 feet by 20 feet to 9 feet by 18 feet, subject to recommendation by the City Engineer and approval by the City Commission. The reduced parking dimensions would only apply where the parking serves the eligible principal use on the same property and is not part of a shared parking area serving other non-eligible uses.
The amendments would also allow up to two feet of a non-residential parking space to overhang into an adjacent landscaped area protected by a raised curb, provided the overhang area is not counted toward required landscaping, buffers, open space, or sidewalk width and remains clear of fixed obstructions. In addition, for the same eligible uses listed above, the City Commission could approve increased spacing between interior landscape islands from an average of every 10 parking spaces to no more than every 15 spaces, upon recommendation of the City Landscape Arborist and City Engineer and provided there is no demonstrated adverse impact on drainage or stormwater management.

The Roadway Improvement Project provides a special benefit to the Tax Parcels located within the Assessment Area, including providing for:safe, adequate, and reliable ingress and egress to all properties, which improves the attractiveness, utilization, marketability, and development potential;

access to and delivery of essential services, including but not limited to fire rescue, emergency medical services, law enforcement, solid waste collection, postal delivery, and transportation of students.
The rate of Assessment for the Project Cost of the Roadway Improvement Project is expressed in terms of "Assigned Acreage," which is a fair and reasonable method of apportionment because Assigned Acreage is a reasonable proxy for the amount of special benefit provided to the assessed properties. description:
The City of Parkland’s (City) Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) establishes the organizational structure, roles, and procedures that guide the City’s response to emergencies and disasters. The plan follows an all‑hazards approach and addresses all phases of emergency management, including prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. It also ensures coordination with federal, state, and county emergency management requirements and compliance with the National Incident Management System (NIMS).
The purpose of the CEMP is to reduce risk to life and property, ensure effective and coordinated emergency response, and support long‑term community recovery following a disaster. The plan serves as a critical operational and coordination tool for City staff, partner agencies, and regional emergency management entities during emergency activations.
The CEMP is intended to be a living document that is reviewed and updated regularly to reflect current organizational structure, contractual services, and points of contact. Regular updates are essential to ensure that information remains accurate and that the City can respond efficiently during an emergency.
The proposed update to the CEMP reflects non‑substantive revisions only, including:
Updates to plan dates and revision history
Identification of the City’s current emergency debris management contractor
Updates to position titles within the City’s organizational structure
Updated contact information for City liaisons to the Broward County Emergency Operations Center (EOC)
These changes are administrative in nature and do not alter the plan’s overall strategy, authority, or operational framework. Approval of the updated CEMP ensures the City remains prepared, coordinated, and compliant with emergency management requirements while maintaining current and accurate emergency response information.

description:
The City of Parkland (City) routinely purchases sports field and athletic facility supplies to support ongoing operations at parks and recreation facilities. These supplies include athletic nets for goals and batting cages, tennis court rollers, baseball and softball field components such as bases and plugs, and other related products necessary for the maintenance, safety, and functionality of City sports amenities. With the development of Wedge Preserve Park, new goals, nets, and other athletic equipment will be required to fully outfit the facility for public use. These items are not included in the construction contract, as it is more cost-effective and operationally beneficial for the City to procure them directly.
The Region 4 Education Service Center Contract No. R250101 (the Contract), awarded to BSN Sports, provides competitively bid, volume discounted pricing for a wide range of athletic equipment and field supplies. Leveraging this contract allows the City to streamline procurement, ensure compliance with purchasing requirements, and obtain lower pricing than would typically be available through standalone quotations.
Region 4 Education Service Center (ESC) issued Request for Proposals Number 25-01 for Athletic, Physical Education Supplies, and Team Uniforms and was competitively solicited through Omnia Partners, allowing authorized public agencies like the City to become a participating entity. Omnia Partners is a nonprofit government purchasing cooperative that reduces the cost of goods and services for agencies by aggregating purchasing power nationwide.
ESC awarded the Contract to BSN Sports LLC. The Contract was executed on June 1, 2025. The term of the Contract is for a period of three (3) years with the right to renew for additional terms up to two (2) years.
In accordance with City Ordnance Code, Section 2-141.7.(e) Cooperative Purchases, the City may "piggyback" a competitively procured contract entered into by another governmental or public entity; and the Code further requires the City Commission to approve contracts exceeding $50,000 per fiscal year.
The Public Works Department is requesting approval to piggyback the Contract for Athletic, Physical Education Supplies, and Team Uniforms in an amount of up to $90,000 for Fiscal Year 2026.

The proposed Interlocal Agreement, attached as Exhibit “1”, is entered into pursuant to Section 163.01, Florida Statutes, also known as the “Florida Interlocal Cooperation Act of 1969”, and other Florida law.

attachments.name: Fast Casual Text Amendment - Staff Memo

description:
The City of Parkland Land Development Code establishes permitted uses for each zoning district. Currently, Full-Service Restaurants and Fast-Food Restaurants are defined and permitted as shown below (Existing Regulations). Importantly, fast-food restaurants are only permitted by Special Exception. Special Exceptions require a separate application, fee, and approval by the City Commission prior to permitting. This process, at a minimum, takes several months to complete the required staff review and meetings before the Planning and Zoning Board and City Commission. To qualify as a Full-Service restaurant, an establishment must provide table service where orders are made from a menu. This precludes any restaurant where orders are taken at a counter or window. Further, food must be prepared for consumption on premises. This precludes establishments from offering to-go orders, except when incidental to the consumption of food on premise.
In addition to the Full-Service and Fast-Food restaurants, a third restaurant category, Fast Casual Restaurants, has emerged over the years and has a growing market share of the restaurant industry. As compared to Fast-Food Restaurants, Fast Casual Restaurants tend to be more upscale establishments, offering customizable menu options that may be served for on, or off-site consumption. They operate more similarly to a full-service restaurant in terms of character and parking generation.
Public Hearings:

description:
The City Commission of the City of Parkland (the “City”) previously adopted Resolution No. 2023-070, which condemned all antisemitism around the world. Antisemitism, including harassment on the basis of actual or perceived Jewish origin, ancestry, ethnicity, identity, affiliation, or faith, remains a persistent, pervasive, and disturbing problem in contemporary American society and in the State of Florida.
The International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (“IHRA”) working definition of “Antisemitism” (the “Definition”) is used by various agencies of the federal and state government, in addition to at least twenty-two States within the United States and an increasing number of cities, and the Definition has also been adopted by at least thirty-seven United Nations member countries, and a growing number of other nations that have Jewish populations. In 2024, the Florida Legislature adopted the IHRA’s working definition of Antisemitism, which is now set forth in Section 1.015, Florida Statutes.
At the January 14, 2026 City Commission Meeting, Commissioner Isrow proposed that the City Commission consider an Ordinance adopting the IHRA definition of antisemitism into the City Code, and received support from other Commissioners to place an item on a future agenda for consideration. The enclosed Ordinance amends Chapter 1 "General Provisions" of the City Code by creating a new Section 1-12 "Adoption of IHRA definition; consideration of antisemitism and hate crimes in enforcing laws." The Ordinance (i) adopts the IHRA definition of antisemitism and the state definition of hate crime and incorporates the defined terms into the City Code, (ii) includes contemporary examples of antisemitism, (iii) requires Parkland City departments and officials to take into consideration the definitions of antisemitism and hate crime for purposes of determining whether an alleged act was motivated by discriminatory anti-Semitic intent, consistent with the federal and state statutes prohibiting hate crimes, and (iv) requires the definitions of Antisemitism and Hate Crime to be used as an educational tool for the purposes of training City employees related to discrimination and anti-bias training. The Ordinance also provides that nothing in the newly created City Code section shall be construed to diminish or infringe upon any right protected under the First Amendment to the Constitution of the United States, or the State of Florida's Constitution, or conflict with Federal or State discrimination laws.

description:
During the Strategic Planning process for the Fiscal Year 2025 Budget, staff was instructed to investigate assessing the cost of roadway improvements to the impacted homeowners. In order to facilitate this process, the City of Parkland (City) hired Government Management Services-South Florida, LLC (GMS) to develop the assessment methodology, and Nabors, Giblin & Nickerson, P.A. to provide the legal guidance and prepare the assessment documents.
At the March 12, 2025 Commission Meeting there was a presentation of the Ranches Roadway Improvements Special Assessment Methodology. Included in the methodology is the legislative findings and case law requirements that support these assessments. The Roadway Improvement Project provides a special benefit to the Tax Parcels located within the Assessment Area, including providing for:safe, adequate, and reliable ingress and egress to all properties, which improves the attractiveness, utilization, marketability, and development potential;
enhanced safety of the roadways by adding guardrails, eliminating potholes, cracks, and uneven surfaces;
protection and/or enhancement of marketability, property and rental values, and the ability to develop property to its highest and best use; and
access to and delivery of essential services, including but not limited to fire rescue, emergency medical services, law enforcement, solid waste collection, postal delivery, and transportation of students.
The rate of Assessment for the Project Cost of the Roadway Improvement Project is expressed in terms of "Assigned Acreage," which is a fair and reasonable method of apportionment because Assigned Acreage is a reasonable proxy for the amount of special benefit provided to the assessed properties. Larger properties have more area to accommodate the additional uses allowed and therefore receive more benefit than smaller properties, even if the additional uses are not currently provided. The Assigned Acreage is determined utilizing the Property Appraiser's Tax Roll acreage data, and rounding down to the nearest half acre.
At the July 8, 2025 Commission Meeting, Capital Project and Related Services Assessment Ordinance 2025-006 was adopted which established the intention of the City and the procedures required to impose special assessments. Approval of the Initial Assessment Resolution presented this evening documents the next steps that will be followed to meet the requirements of the City's Code. The process includes notifying all impacted parties by first class mail, as well as publication of the required notices in advance of the Public Hearing that is scheduled for December 3, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

At the October 8, 2025 Commission Meeting there was a presentation of the Pine Tree Estates Roadway Improvements Special Assessment Methodology. Included in the methodology is the legislative findings and case law requirements that support these assessments. The Roadway Improvement Project provides a special benefit to the Tax Parcels located within the Assessment Area, including providing for:safe, adequate, and reliable ingress and egress to all properties, which improves the attractiveness, utilization, marketability, and development potential;
enhanced safety of the roadways by adding guardrails, eliminating potholes, cracks, and uneven surfaces;
protection and/or enhancement of marketability, property and rental values, and the ability to develop property to its highest and best use; and
access to and delivery of essential services, including but not limited to fire rescue, emergency medical services, law enforcement, solid waste collection, postal delivery, and transportation of students.
The rate of Assessment for the Project Cost of the Roadway Improvement Project is expressed in terms of "Buildable Lots," which is a fair and reasonable method of apportionment because the number of Buildable Lots is a reasonable proxy for the amount of special benefit provided to the assessed properties. The majority (96%) of the Assessment Area consists of similarly sized residential Tax Parcels of 1.75 acres or less on which only one (1) Dwelling Unit may be sited, pursuant to the City's current land development regulations. Given that all such Dwelling Units produce about the same number of vehicular trips on an average, annual basis, they should similarly benefit from the Project. Accordingly, it is fair and reasonable to assign all such Tax Parcels one (1) Buildable Lot regardless of minor variations in property sizes. There are 11 Tax Parcels with an Assessment Area greater than 1.75 acres in size such that additional Single-Family Residential Units may feasibly be sited, even if the additional use is not currently provided. Therefore, it is fair and reasonable to charge two (2) Buildable Lots to those 11 Tax Parcels based on their highest and best possible use.
There is a Tax Parcel of Utility Property within the Assessment Area that does have ingress and egress access via a road that is included in the Project. However, it is only accessed on a limited basis. It is therefore fair and reasonable to assign one (1) Buildable Lot to that Utility Parcel based on the assumption that it will have approximately the same number of vehicular trips as a residential property. Tax Parcels that only utilize Holmberg Road for ingress and egress, such as the northern Utility Property and the Estates of Pine Tree neighborhood, are not included in the Assessment.
At the July 8, 2025 Commission Meeting, Capital Project and Related Services Assessment Ordinance 2025-006 was adopted which established the intention of the City and the procedures required to impose special assessments. Approval of the Initial Assessment Resolution presented this evening documents the next steps that will be followed to meet the requirements of the City's Code. The process includes notifying all impacted parties by first class mail, as well as publication of the required notices in advance of the Public Hearing that is scheduled for December 3, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

Staff is seeking approval of purchases of goods and services from the Amazon Online Market Place via the piggyback of OMNIA Partners, Prince William County Public Schools Contract #R-TC-17006.
This contract was competitively solicited via Omnia Partners, a nonprofit government purchasing cooperative that aggregates purchasing power to reduce costs for public agencies. Price William County Public Schools issued RFP #R-TC-17006, Online Marketplace for Purchases of Products and Services, which was issued on September 14, 2016. A total of twelve (12) responses were received with a contract being awarded to Amazon Online Marketplace on January 19, 2017. The initial term of the contract was five (5) years, with options to renew for three (3) additional two (2) year periods. The contract currently expires January 18, 2028.
The Amazon Online Marketplace has proven to be both an effective and efficient purchasing platform for staff to leverage for a diverse range of City requirements. The highly competitive environment of the Amazon Online Marketplace promotes favorable pricing and delivery terms for the City.
The estimated twelve-month City-wide spend on the Amazon Online Marketplace is approximately $175,000. This amount has been budgeted and available for the various expenditures until the end of the current fiscal year.
Procurement Code Section 2-141.5 requires City Commission approval of purchases of goods or services from the same vendor exceeding the aggregate sum of $50,000 per twelve-month period or $150,000 on a multi-year basis.
The City believes it is in the best interest of the City to authorize purchases of goods and services from Amazon Online Marketplace via the piggyback of OMNIA Partners, Prince William County Public Schools Contract #R-TC-17006, in the aggregate amount of $175,000 until the end of the current fiscal year.
title:
Resolution 2025-071: Purchases of Goods and Services from Amazon Online Marketplace
A Resolution of the City Commission of the City of Parkland, Florida, approving purchases of goods and services from Amazon Online Marketplace, via the piggyback of OMNIA Partners, Prince William County Public Schools Contract #R-TC-17006, in the aggregate amount of $175,000 through the end of the current fiscal year; providing for execution; providing for an effective date.

description:
The City of Parkland (the “City”), requires professional services from an experienced firm to administer the City’s Planning Department and provide Planning Director services for Fiscal Year 2026.
The scope of required services (the “Services”) will include daily Planning Director functions regarding land use and zoning matters, as well as special projects such as updating the City’s Water Supply Plan, Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Regulations, and providing planning services for the City’s Village in the Park Project.
Complete Cities Planning Group, LLC, (the "Consultant") has provided a work authorization (attached as Exhibits “A" and “A-1”) to perform the necessary Services, in the amount of $98,000. Services rendered will be at an hourly rate (see attached “Exhibit B”) in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Agreement for Professional Services between the City and DRMP, Inc. via Resolution 2023-022 ("Exhibit C"). The Consultant is a subconsultant to that contract.
Pursuant to Section 2-141.5 of the City's Code of Ordinances, purchases of $50,000 or more with the same vendor require City Commission approval.
Staff is requesting approval of the work authorization from the Consultant to provide the necessary Services for the amount of $98,000.
